work.starts: mango tree and a goat

rows: both are living: they need food, water and air, they grow, they reproduce and they react to their surroundings
makes its own food in its leaves; stays in one place; has roots and leaves; no mouth or legs
eats plants for food; moves from place to place; has a mouth, legs and a backbone; breathes with lungs

work.starts: How many vertebrae are in your backbone

blocks.en: A human being is born with 33 vertebrae: 7 in the neck, 12 in the chest, 5 in the lower back, 5 joined together in the sacrum and 4 joined at the tail end (coccyx). In an adult some of these have joined, so about 26 separate bones are counted.

work.starts: Complete the table

rows: protect the heart and the lungs
hold and pick up things; help us write, lift and throw
hold up the body and help us walk and run

work.starts: Take two soft plants having white flowers

blocks.en: After a few hours the petals and veins of the plant standing in red ink turn pink or red; the other plant stays white. The roots took in the coloured water and the stem carried it up (through its water tubes) to the leaves and flowers. So the stem carries water from the roots to the other parts of the plant.

work.starts: Sow few seeds in it

blocks.en: A seed holds stored food. The baby plant lives on this food until its leaves grow and can make food for it (photosynthesis). So the plant first grows from the food of the seed, and later from the food made by its own leaves.

work.starts: Identify the environment of the animals
Enter the living things given below
Complete the following food chains

items.en: The arrow means "is eaten by"; every chain starts with a plant (the producer).

work.starts: Pour clean water in two glasses

blocks.en: I would drink the clean water. The muddy (turbid) water has dirt and germs in it, which cause diarrhoea, typhoid and cholera, so drinking water must be clean and, if it is not sure, boiled.

work.starts: Take a cup of water and pour it into a glass

blocks.en: The volume of the water is the same in the glass as it was in the cup (if none is spilt): a liquid has a fixed volume.

work.starts: Pour water in three vessels having different shapes

blocks.en: The shape of the water is different in each vessel: it takes the shape of the vessel that holds it. A liquid has no shape of its own, but its volume stays the same.

work.starts: Take balloons of three different shapes

blocks.en: The inflated balloons keep three different shapes. The air in each takes the shape of the balloon that holds it, so a gas has no fixed shape; it fills its container.

work.starts: Tie a balloon not inflated at one end

blocks.en: The end with the inflated balloon bends down, because the air inside has weight (mass), so the inflated balloon is heavier. This shows that air, a gas, has weight.

work.starts: Which object has occupied more space

blocks.en: The football occupies the most space (it has the largest volume); the pen occupies the least. Everything that is matter has weight and takes up space.

work.starts: Put a piece of wood in a cloth bag

blocks.en: The wooden piece cannot come out of the small hole because it is a solid: a solid has a fixed shape and size, and the piece is bigger than the hole.

work.starts: Pour water in a plastic bag and tie a knot

items.en: 1. The water flows out through the hole at the bottom and falls down: a liquid flows and has no shape of its own.
2. When you press the soft bottle full of water, the water is not squeezed into a smaller space: it hardly changes its volume. (If the bottle has a hole, the water squirts out.)

work.starts: Put few objects such as steel spoon

rows: not hot: plastic is a poor conductor
not hot (or only slightly): wood is a poor conductor

work.starts: Put a brick on one pan of the balance

blocks.en: The balance tilts towards the brick: the pan with the brick goes down. The foam is bigger but the brick has more matter packed into its space, so it has more mass and weighs more.

work.starts: Light a candle or lamp in a dark room

blocks.en: A dark shadow of the hand appears on the wall. The hand is opaque and does not let light pass, and light travels in straight lines, so it cannot bend round the hand.

work.starts: Prism is a three-dimensional transparent object

blocks.en: On the wall or paper you see a band of seven colours in this order: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet (a spectrum, like a rainbow). So white sunlight is a mixture of these colours, and the prism splits it.

work.starts: Strike/ring the school bell strongly

blocks.en: The bell gives a loud sound. If you touch the ringing bell you feel it trembling (vibrating), and when you hold it still the sound stops. So sound is made by vibrations; the energy of your hand is changed into sound energy.

work.starts: Fix a torch bulb in a holder

blocks.en: With the switch ON the circuit is closed, so electric current flows from the cell through the wires and the bulb, and the bulb glows (electrical energy changes into light and heat). With the switch OFF the circuit is open and the bulb goes off.

work.starts: Which force (push or pull) will be applied

rows: Force used to change its shape

work.starts: Tie a pencil to a piece of thread

blocks.en: Yes, gravity is acting on the pencil all the time: it pulls the pencil down, and the thread holds it up. When the thread is broken, the pencil falls to the ground, because gravity, the pull of the Earth, draws everything towards the Earth.

work.starts: Stretch a paper sheet on a hardboard

blocks.en: Writing on paper is easy; on the plastic sheet the pen slips and the ink does not stay. The paper is rough, so the pen grips it (more friction); the plastic is smooth, so the pen slides over it with little friction. Friction is the force that opposes the movement of two surfaces that touch.

work.starts: Take a ruler, a pencil and a book

blocks.en: A small force on the far end of the ruler lifts the book. The ruler works as a lever, the pencil is its fulcrum (pivot) and the book is the load. The lever is easier to use when the pencil is nearer the book. A lever is a simple machine.

work.starts: Which minerals are used to make the items
Identify the climate (dry, mild, desert and snow)

rows: a meadow of flowers under a cloudy sky

work.starts: Take a globe and throw torch light on it

blocks.en: It is day on the half of the globe that faces the torch and night on the other half. As the globe turns, a place goes from day to night and back again. This shows that the rotation of the Earth on its axis (once in about 24 hours) causes day and night.

work.starts: Fix a stick at this location in the ground

rows: very short (towards the north in Pakistan)

blocks.en: Yes, the shadow changes in length and direction during the day. The Sun seems to move across the sky because the Earth rotates; when it is low the shadow is long, when it is high (noon) the shadow is shortest.

work.starts: Pass a long needle through a rubber ball

blocks.en: The ball (Earth) is tilted, and the tilt always points the same way as it goes round the bulb (Sun). In some positions the northern half leans towards the bulb and gets more direct light (summer there); in the opposite position it leans away (winter there); in between come spring and autumn. So the Earth's yearly journey round the Sun, with its tilted axis, makes the seasons.

work.starts: Place a torch, a football and a tennis ball in one line

blocks.en: Yes: the shadow of the football (Earth) falls on the tennis ball (Moon), which goes dark. This is a lunar eclipse: it happens when the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon and the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon (at full moon).

work.starts: place the tennis ball nearer to the football

blocks.en: The shadow of the tennis ball (Moon) falls on a small spot of the football (Earth). This is a solar eclipse: it happens when the Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth (at new moon) and its shadow falls on a part of the Earth; only the people in that shadow see the Sun covered.

work.starts: 100°F fever

blocks.en: A normal body temperature is about 98.6 °F (37 °C). A fever of 100 °F means the body temperature is 100 °F, higher than normal: the person has a mild fever, should rest, drink water and be shown to a doctor if it goes on or rises.
